reason: The whole case requires an anonymous object-constructor expression (anonObj = object { ... }), which is not covered by the supported Expressions list. This makes it a feature case even though it mixes that construct with supported class/type/function/constant/variable declarations, new expressions, mapping/list constructors, assignments and returns. The intended negative checks concern non-public types exposed through public fields and signatures; no explicit access-level exclusion is stated for the otherwise supported declarations.
unsupported_constructs: Anonymous object-constructor expression initializing anonObj: object { public string s = ""; public Baz z = 1; public Foo foo1 = new; }. This is distinct from the listed new expression and from an object type descriptor.
test_design_notes: The unsupported anonymous object constructor occurs on an unmarked line, so it can introduce a diagnostic unrelated to the marked access-level checks.

Several declarations carry multiple @error markers on one line (fooFunc2, fooFunc3, BazFunc, test6 and test7); these encode multiple expected diagnostics at a shared location. No obvious malformed marker is present.
The isolated initializer is expressly covered by isolated function support; it is not itself a reason to classify the case as a feature.
